items.item: Applications implement the specification and rules board through a recognizable shared information hierarchy, typography, scientific symbols and caption treatments; carrier-specific rearrangement is allowed.

The four themes have distinct visual treatments within the shared institution-based system, and each theme's identifier and scientific visual language remain recognizable in its corresponding diagram or digital adaptation.
Each digital adaptation retains its corresponding poster's program block, learning-question meaning, causal explanation and scientific relationship while adapting the composition to its carrier.

requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

A single specification page defines the series' information order, placement for each carrier, font families, weights and minimum sizes. It records 594 × 841 mm A1 trim, 3 mm bleed, at least 5 mm internal safety, #18324A, and the full wording of both disclosure labels. Missing categories or contradictory values fail; the organization and chosen typefaces are flexible.

The board visibly demonstrates a master visual, four distinguishable theme identifiers, type treatments, scientific symbols and caption styling that implement the specification. It prints the program name, 594 × 841 mm, #18324A, 'Schematic — not to scale' and 'Distance scale in AU; body symbols not to scale'. Composition may vary; omitted components or conflicts with the specification fail.

Each target explicitly reproduces the specification's 594 × 841 mm dimensions, #18324A code and complete wording of both scale disclosures. Clear text within a reused specification page counts in the presentation. Paraphrased disclosures, missing facts or inconsistent values fail.

Assess the portrait poster trim and artwork relative to the specified physical geometry. Edge-reaching artwork extends through the 3 mm bleed, while text, the institution mark and essential diagram content remain at least 5 mm inside trim. Larger internal margins are allowed. Intrusion into the protected area or missing required bleed fails; do not assess exact raster pixel counts.

Read each program block. Moon roles pair the program and institution names with The changing Moon and January–March 2027; eclipse roles with When shadows align and April–June 2027; seasons roles with One tilt, two seasons and July–September 2027; distance roles with A ruler for space and October–December 2027. Original name and title words are required, with flexible capitalization and line breaks; unambiguous equivalent date typography is allowed. Missing, mismatched or event-date interpretations of the quarterly records fail.

Each image explains that sunlight illuminates half the Moon and orbital motion changes how much of that half an Earth observer sees, with an approximately 29.5-day cycle. Show new Moon, waxing crescent, first quarter, waxing gibbous, full Moon, waning gibbous, last quarter and waning crescent in a readable sequence. Identify the Earth viewpoint and Northern Hemisphere convention, with corresponding right-lit waxing and left-lit waning appearances. A labelled outline for new Moon and paraphrased explanations are allowed. Missing phases, reversed sequence, incompatible illumination or an Earth-shadow explanation for ordinary phases fail.

Each image includes explicitly named solar and lunar examples and labels Sun, Earth and Moon. The solar arrangement places the Moon between Sun and Earth and shows its shadow reaching part of Earth; the lunar arrangement places Earth between Sun and Moon and shows Earth's shadow reaching the Moon. Explain that the lunar orbital plane is tilted relative to Earth's orbital plane, so suitable alignments occur only occasionally. Rotation, diagram orientation and exaggerated sizes are allowed; reversed body order, shadow direction or an implication of eclipses every orbit fails. The standalone diagram also carries its corresponding theme title.

June and December configurations preserve an approximately parallel Earth axis. Written hemisphere and season labels pair northern summer with southern winter around June and reverse those seasons around December. Explain how axial tilt produces more direct sunlight in the hemisphere experiencing summer and winter in the opposite hemisphere. Diagram orientation and explanatory exaggeration may vary; changing the axial direction between positions, reversing the pairings or attributing seasons to Earth–Sun distance fails.

Each ruler identifies an astronomical unit as approximately the mean Earth–Sun distance, about 150 million kilometres, and represents mean orbital distances from the Sun. Label Sun at 0 AU, Earth at 1 AU and Saturn at 9.5 AU, with Earth positioned about 1/9.5 of the Sun-to-Saturn span on one unbroken linear scale. Print 'Distance scale in AU; body symbols not to scale' in full. Symbol sizes and ruler orientation are flexible; equal spacing, logarithmic or broken scales, incorrect values or missing disclosure fail. The standalone diagram also prints its corresponding theme title.

Every schematic figure or clearly grouped schematic comparison has an associated 'Schematic — not to scale' disclosure. Embedded diagrams retain the same disclosure as standalone equivalents. Solar versus lunar examples and northern versus southern hemispheres are distinguished with words, supported by symbols and color. A shared caption may cover a clearly bounded paired figure; an unrelated label elsewhere or color-only distinctions fail. Linear AU rulers use their dedicated distance disclosure; an additional schematic disclosure is required only for separate schematic geometry.

Each application contains a learning question, a causal explanation and a diagram that teaches its assigned relationship. Moon asks why the visible bright shape changes; eclipse asks how solar and lunar eclipses differ; seasons asks why northern and southern seasons differ; distance asks how one unit describes very large distances. Rephrasing and carrier-specific rearrangement are allowed while preserving these meanings and the complete teaching content. Decorative astronomy imagery alone, an omitted question or an explanation reduced to a topic label fails.

Screens use landscape composition and social posts use square composition. All copy and the institution mark remain inside a protected region inset by 5% of the corresponding width or height from each edge. Larger insets are allowed and backgrounds may extend to the edges. Incorrect carrier shape or protected content entering the outer inset fails; exact pixel dimensions are not assessed.

Review the complete video and its duration. It runs for 10 seconds, begins with the solar example and ends with the lunar example. The complete program block remains legible throughout, and the screen's wording and labels are retained. Motion and intermediate transitions are flexible; a blank or unrelated endpoint, disappearing program block, changed copy or incorrect duration fails.

requirementChecks.criteria: Across the video, explicitly label the three bodies and distinguish the solar and lunar examples. Solar eclipse geometry shows the Moon between Sun and Earth with the Moon's shadow reaching Earth; lunar geometry shows Earth between Sun and Moon with Earth's shadow reaching the Moon. Retain the explanation that tilted orbital planes limit eclipse alignments. Sequential presentation is allowed; reversed arrangements, incorrect shadow motion or omitted orbital explanation fails.

requirementChecks.criteria: The presentation has eight or more pages and an application map that names where each quarterly program record, required scientific relationship and exact scale disclosure appears. Coverage includes the four themes, relevant standalone diagrams, digital versions and eclipse animation. Tables, annotated thumbnails or prose mappings are acceptable; a generic inventory without fact-to-application links or omitted required mappings fails.

Find identifiable visible reuse of every listed source, including specification content, the board, all four posters, both diagrams, all four digital adaptations and frames from the delivered animation. Scaled reproductions and contextual mockups are allowed if the original work remains identifiable. Text-only mentions, substitute artwork or omission of any source fails.
